policy.title: Theorem 21.15.1 requires tropical equidistribution and canonical-measure inputs
policy.text: Let K be the function field of an integral projective variety over an algebraically closed constant field, regular in codimension one, with product formula defined by an ample class. The abelian variety A is totally degenerate at the chosen place, and the analytic comparison uses the completed algebraic closure there. In this setting, assume tropical purity and finite polytopality in the relevant dimensions, positive top-cell Lebesgue densities of the normalized canonical tropical measures, zero mass on lower-dimensional polyhedral sets, and equidistribution of generic small nets for the ample symmetric canonical polarizations on the product and its difference-map image. The locally proved generic finiteness of the difference map then gives the dimension comparison and the diagonal mass contradiction for a positive-dimensional integral X with finite stabilizer. The normalized measure identity uses equidistribution on both sides. The manuscript does not establish the required tropical and arithmetic inputs internally. The subsequent full torsion-translate conclusion also uses the totally degenerate quotient and zero-trace theorems.
policy.evidence: Section 21.15 states three Gubler inputs before the theorem. In the proof, equidistribution gives the normalized pushforward identity and the density statements give positive product mass and zero image mass. See Gubler, Tropical varieties, Theorem 1.3, and Bogomolov, Theorem 5.5 and Section 6.

policy.title: Native construction of the mixed current
policy.text: On a boundaryless analytic space, the statement assumes continuous potentials locally uniformly approximable by original smooth psh functions on a fixed open neighbourhood and 0 ≤ m ≤ n. The required positive (m,m)-current is the weak limit of products of the smooth approximants, independent of their choice and compatible with restriction, and is a measure in top degree. The displayed obligation names CLD 2012, Corollary 5.6.5, as the imported result. The native recursion still requires multiplier convergence in the relevant test category. Positivity of the individual curvature currents alone does not supply the local approximation hypothesis.
policy.evidence: Section 11.1, after the theorem The mixed product constructed in CLD 2012. RC2 explicitly requires a native mixed-current proof and identifies open multiplier convergence.

policy.title: Frame independence and the scalar Poincaré–Lelong identity
policy.text: For a finite continuous metric, frame independence requires vanishing curvature for the logarithmic absolute value of a unit. The displayed formula for an algebraic variety and a nonzero meromorphic section additionally requires the divisor current for the logarithmic absolute value, with c₁ equal to the curvature of the negative log norm of the section plus the divisor current. The manuscript supplies CLD 2012, Theorem 4.6.5, or the cited Gubler alternative for this step. A native replacement must cover the stated algebraic setting, meromorphic sections, sign convention and test sheaf.
policy.evidence: Section 11.1, after Frame independence and the Poincaré–Lelong sign. RC2 explicitly opens the scalar divisor/current identity.

policy.title: Local smooth psh approximation from current positivity
policy.text: The proved implication starts with local uniform approximation by original smooth psh functions and concludes positivity of the limiting curvature current. The converse for an arbitrary continuous current-psh function remains unsupported here. When an argument requires smooth approximants on a fixed neighbourhood, it must assume or independently establish their existence. General functoriality of continuous current-psh functions is a separate assertion.
policy.evidence: The remark What the 2012 construction does not establish identifies the converse and points to CLD 2012, Remark 5.6.4.

policy.title: Multiplier convergence in the original smooth test category
policy.text: The assertion is weak convergence of uⱼTⱼ to uT when ordinary positive currents Tⱼ of fixed bidegree converge weakly and continuous uⱼ converge locally uniformly. The required native density statement is uniform approximation near the test support in the relevant category. It remains an input to the one-step positivity argument and the iteration in the next section.
policy.evidence: RC2 immediately after Multiplication and weak convergence cites CLD 2012, Corollaries 5.4.7–5.4.8, as the density input.

policy.title: The toric Gauss-section comparison is imported
policy.text: For a toric line bundle on a normal toric variety with complete rational fan over an algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field, the section uses Gubler–Hertel's classification of continuous semipositive toric metrics including boundary extension. It also assumes that the tropical pushforward of the Chern measure is the real Monge–Ampère measure of f = −ψ and that the analytic measure is obtained by pushing this real measure along the toric Gauss section. The preceding real polyhedral calculation computes the real measure only. The analytic identity on tests that do not factor through tropicalization remains an imported input.
policy.evidence: Section 21.7 calls the displayed comparison an imported analytic comparison theorem and singles out the Gauss-section equality.

policy.title: The polyhedral description of canonical measures
policy.text: For the stated discretely valued source setting after passage to the completed algebraic closure, this theorem gives a finite tropical simplex description and a relative Lebesgue decomposition of the canonical mixed measure. The allowed simplex dimensions use both toric rank and the dimension of the good-reduction abelian part. Strict positivity is asserted for ample factors. The native proof of the full description remains an explicit obligation. A support consequence proved after assuming the description does not discharge that obligation.
